$comment: [[D-FFI-DIRENT-API-DECLARED-OVER-VOID-NOT-ITS-OWN-STRUCTS]] — the runnable half of the closure. THE DEFECT: dirent.json declared its whole API over `void` (`opendir :: fn(ptr<char>) -> ptr<void>`, `readdir :: fn(ptr<void>) -> ptr<void>`, `closedir :: fn(ptr<void>) -> i32`) while the SAME file already declared, correctly and per format, both types those signatures are about — an opaque `DIR` typedef and a `struct dirent` with elf/pe/macho variants. So the descriptor mechanism that exists to TYPE a shipped library's surface asserted nothing about this one, and `int *x = readdir(d);` compiled clean here where POSIX, glibc and mingw-w64 all diagnose it. ★★ WHY THE SIBLING EXAMPLE COULD NOT CATCH IT: `examples/c/shipped_dirent_readdir` walks a real directory and matches "." by d_name, and it passed on all four legs throughout — C converts `void *` to `struct dirent *` silently, so an ordinary walk is blind to the return type by construction. The discriminating question is the type of the CALL EXPRESSION, and `sizeof(*readdir(d))` is the one form that asks it: unevaluated, so nothing is consumed, and answering `sizeof(void)` (1, or a hard refusal) versus the platform record. ★ AGNOSTIC BY CONSTRUCTION — the manifest names four legs whose `struct dirent` is 280 (glibc x86_64 and aarch64, MEASURED via the real headers: d_ino u64@0, d_off i64@8, d_reclen u16@16, d_type u8@18, d_name char[256]@19), 268 (pe/mingw-w64, MEASURED with mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 native: d_ino i32@0, d_reclen u16@4, d_namlen u16@6, d_name char[260]@8, align 4) and 1048 (Darwin 64-bit-inode), and NOT ONE of those numbers appears in the source: both sides of the comparison derive from the declared type. ★ THE pe LEG IS THE ONE THAT BINDS THE DECLARATION TO A BODY DSS ITSELF SHIPS — Windows has no POSIX directory API in any platform image, so `realization.pe.source` names `runtime/platform/src/dirent.c`, that unit `#include`s this very header, and its three definitions now spell `DIR *opendir(const char *)` / `struct dirent *readdir(DIR *)` / `int closedir(DIR *)` verbatim. The agreement between the ABI DSS publishes and the bytes DSS writes is therefore checked BY THE COMPILER on every pe build: retype the descriptor and that translation unit stops compiling. RED-ON-DISABLE (REMOVE direction, over the shipped descriptor; no rebuild needed — the config snapshot is taken at ctest RUN time): restore `dirent.json`'s `readdir` row to "fn(ptr<void>) -> ptr<void>" and this example reds on every leg while `shipped_dirent_readdir` stays green, which is exactly the attribution split that makes this entry worth its own directory.
